newsitem.title: FRANCE: France boosts Serbia opposition, raps repression.
newsitem.headline: France boosts Serbia opposition, raps repression.

text.p: France condemed police repression against pro-democracy protesters in Belgrade and officially recognised the leaders of Serbia's opposition in a significant policy switch on Monday, inviting them for talks in Paris.

The Foreign Ministry said France believed it could play a useful role in promoting a dialogue between hardline socialist President Slobodan Milosevic and the leaders of the Zajedno democratic opposition coalition.
Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said in a statement he had invited opposition leaders Zoran Djindjic, Vuk Draskovic and Vesna Pesic to come to Paris as soon as possible.
"This invitation amounts to recognition by the French government of the leaders of the Zajedno opposition coalition, which through the past weeks has proved its political maturity," he said.

De Charette said France condemned "with the utmost firmness" Sunday's police violence against peaceful demonstrators who have been protesting for 78 days against alleged fraud by Milosevic's government in municipal elections.
"(France) solemnly warns the Serbian authorities against a slide into violence which can only lead to a disastrous outcome for their country," he said.
Germany and Britain also condemned the violence.
The explicit recognition of the opposition was a change from Paris's previously cautious stance on the crisis.
Foreign ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said: "Our concern is to get a dialogue started between the opposition and the government. We think we can play a useful role."

De Charette said a report by former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez on behalf of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), upholding the opposition victory in last year's disputed municipal elections, offered the only chance of a political solution.

"France is ready for its part to work for this last-chance reconciliation. Exhorting the authorities to adopt the path of dialogue and not of violence, it wants to contribute to opening this dialogue," his statement said.
Pesic visited Paris last month and met de Charette. But she was then a guest of the opposition Socialist party, not of the centre-right government.

Diplomats said France had been among European Union states most reluctant to clash with Milosevic early in the Belgrade crisis, arguing that the Serbian president, despite his flaws, had a key role in consolidating fragile peace in the Balkans.
